title: Identifying Feed-Forward Hawkes Networks from Binned Counts at a Fixed Bin Width
banked_reason: Operator stop: sound point-process identifiability, but no causal anchor. Zero occurrences of do/intervention/confounding/causal-sufficiency/potential-outcome in the core; none of its 20 assumptions is causal; all 19 references are point-process, time-series or matrix-analysis. Recovering G(A) is Granger-style structure identification whose causal reading needs a causal-sufficiency assumption the paper never states and a literature it never cites.
tldr: At every fixed known bin width \(\Delta>0\), coarse timestamping does not erase the labeled Hawkes mechanism in the stated feed-forward model: the mean and two positive covariance lags recover \(\operatorname{im}(A)\), the common decay, every amplitude, the baselines, and hence \(G(A)\), including singular matrices, repeated poles, disconnected components, diamonds, and proportional rows. A broader exact population theorem covers every nonzero stable common-exponential mechanism whose generator restricted to \(\operatorname{im}(A)\) lies in the principal-log strip, including feedback, self-excitation, and reciprocal edges. Its inverse first reconstructs the complete covariance response from the two lags and then uses a finite matrix-resolvent calculation plus one uniquely characterized positive scalar root; Wiener--Hopf uniqueness certifies that root but is not an unevaluated computational step. The covariance-only map first recovers \(D\) and the mean from \(\Gamma_0\). The empty graph is exactly the \(\beta\)-nonidentified stratum. Rank-adaptive estimation, vanishing-threshold support recovery, and conservative simultaneous graph confidence sets remain proved only for the acyclic margin class. One-lag injectivity on the named three-node motifs and honest adaptation over the nuisance-regular closure remain open.
gap: Published Hawkes identification results use the entire continuous covariance function, full spectral or Laplace-transform information, latent-time likelihood, higher cumulants, the full aggregated-count distribution, or a vanishing-mesh discrete approximation. Koyama2025 is the closest fixed-bin second-order method, but page 8, Theorem 2 and Equation (18), and Corollary 1 establish an \(O(\Delta t^3)\) small-bin spectral approximation for a coarse-grained process rather than an exact finite-lag inverse for the original process. Kirchner2016 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Equation (21), establishes \(N^{(\Delta)}\Rightarrow N\) as \(\Delta\to0\), and Section 3.3, Equations (25)--(28), compares lag structures without furnishing a fixed-positive-bin inverse.
fill: The project derives the exact bin-covariance semigroup, proves the image identity, performs a basis-invariant restricted logarithm, recovers edge direction from the skew jump, and characterizes \(A=0\) as the exact reason for excluding the nonidentified decay stratum. Rank-adaptive estimation and simultaneous graph uncertainty propagate the raw-moment HAC law through the same correctly centered composite Jacobian \(\mathcal J(\theta)=D(\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\). The formal targets separate vanishing-threshold support selection from fixed-level sign inversion with a uniform \(\liminf\) coverage lower bound. A finite-depth immigration--birth argument derives uniform geometric mixing and an explicit eighth-bin-count moment constant from primitive margins; boundary honesty remains open only over \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), where decay, parameter, intensity, variance, mixing, moment, and HAC regularity remain controlled while rank, edge strength, and \(A=0\) may approach the boundary.
